name: Loose Watercolour
name_th: สีน้ำแบบลื่นไหล
historical_background: Watercolour is a semi-transparent paint of pigment in a water-soluble binder, usually on paper, where the unpainted paper supplies the light (Tate, 'Watercolour'). Tate's examples run from Turner's The Blue Rigi, Sunrise (1842) to Klee (1927); the loose, wet-into-wet manner is a long-standing practice of plein-air sketchers rather than a named movement.
visual_characteristics: Transparent washes, soft blooms and backruns, white paper left as highlights, edges that dissolve into the page.
line_characteristics: Few or no outlines; edges come from wash boundaries; occasional dry-brush or thin pen accents.
shape_language: Suggestive, broken silhouettes; lost-and-found edges; big simple masses.
color_characteristics: Limited palette (3–5 pigments), colours mixed on the paper, granulation in blues and earths, high value range from paper white.
lighting_characteristics: Light is the paper itself; soft diffuse daylight reads best; strong darks used sparingly.
texture_characteristics: Cold-press paper tooth, pigment granulation, hard dried edges (cauliflowers) where wet meets damp.
composition_characteristics: Large quiet wash areas plus one sharp focal zone; vignetted edges fading to white paper.
emotional_characteristics: Fresh, airy, spontaneous, gentle; can turn melancholic in grey palettes.
time_optic_fit: Good for soft backgrounds and seasonal moods behind a real frame photo; poor for showing frame detail itself (washes blur hinges and lens edges), so keep the product as a photo/cutout layer on top.
common_mistakes: muddy watercolour from too many overlapping colours
uniform digital blur passing as wash
no white paper left, everything tinted
outlined cartoon plus watercolour fill that looks like colouring-book
AI text-like scribbles in the washes
prompt_template: Loose transparent watercolour painting of {subject} in {setting}, wet-into-wet washes with soft blooms, white paper left for highlights, limited {palette} palette, {lighting}, {composition}, visible cold-press paper texture, edges fading into the white page, no text.
prompt_example: Loose transparent watercolour painting of a small corner optical shop in a quiet Bangkok soi in the morning, wet-into-wet washes with soft blooms, white paper left for highlights, limited palette of deep green, warm grey and a touch of peach, soft overcast daylight, shop placed on the left third with a large calm sky wash, visible cold-press paper texture, edges fading into the white page, no text.
avoid_phrases: in the style of <any living artist>
flux_notes: FLUX.1 schnell tends to produce a clean 'digital watercolour' with tidy edges and splatter clichés; ask for 'granulation', 'hard dried edges', 'white paper' and lower detail. img2img at denoise ~0.55 over a simple sketch keeps structure.

name: Botanical Watercolour
name_th: สีน้ำพฤกษศาสตร์
historical_background: Botanical illustration grew from herbals and scientific plant records, where accuracy of form, colour and structure mattered more than mood. The controlled, layered watercolour approach is craft practice; no museum page was opened for this entry, so details are given as practice, not history.
visual_characteristics: Single specimen on white, precise contours, glazed layers building form, every vein and petal edge resolved.
line_characteristics: Fine graphite underdrawing kept invisible or very faint; edges defined by colour, not ink.
shape_language: Organic but exact; true proportions; leaves and stems as rhythmic curves.
color_characteristics: Faithful local colour built in thin glazes; subtle temperature shifts in shadows; no artistic recolouring.
lighting_characteristics: Even, soft, conventionally from upper left; gentle cast shadow or none.
texture_characteristics: Smooth hot-press paper, almost invisible brush marks, dry-brush for fuzz and veins.
composition_characteristics: Isolated specimen with generous white margin; sometimes detail insets of seed, flower section.
time_optic_fit: Fits as a decorative layer (leaves around a frame photo, nature-themed lens info) and suits the trusted-expert tone; not for scenes or people.
common_mistakes: impossible plant anatomy (wrong leaf count, fused petals)
loud splatter added to 'make it watercolour'
prompt_template: Botanical watercolour study of {subject}, precise contours, thin layered glazes, accurate structure, {palette}, {lighting}, {composition}, isolated on white hot-press paper with generous margins, no text, no labels.
prompt_example: Botanical watercolour study of a sprig of jasmine and pandan leaves arranged as a frame border, precise contours, thin layered glazes, accurate structure, fresh greens with creamy whites, soft even light from upper left, empty centre space for a glasses photo, isolated on white hot-press paper with generous margins, no text, no labels.
avoid_phrases: in the style of <any living artist>
vintage botanical print with latin labels
flux_notes: Usually good at clean botanical layouts but invents labels and pseudo-latin text; always add 'no text, no labels'. Leaf anatomy errors are common; check counts.

name: Flat Gouache
name_th: สีกวอชแบนเรียบ
historical_background: Gouache is a water-soluble paint that, unlike watercolour, is opaque: more binder and added inert pigment such as chalk build a covering layer (Tate, 'Gouache'). Its matte, even coverage made it a long-time medium for designers' layouts and posters.
visual_characteristics: Opaque matte colour shapes, crisp edges, minimal gradients, slight hand-made unevenness.
line_characteristics: Edges formed by shape meeting shape; occasional thin brush line; no hard black outline.
shape_language: Simplified, geometric-organic shapes; clear silhouettes; designed rather than observed.
color_characteristics: Limited flat palette of 4–6 mixed colours, light over dark possible, chalky matte finish.
lighting_characteristics: Light shown as one or two flat value steps; cast shadows as solid shapes.
texture_characteristics: Faint brush streaks, dry edges, paper grain under thin areas.
composition_characteristics: Graphic, poster-like; strong figure-ground; room for type.
time_optic_fit: Strong fit for carousels and tip posts; matches brand flat colours well (phthalo green, peach accent). Frame details must be simplified or kept as a photo layer.
common_mistakes: vector-perfect fills that lose the paint feel
glossy highlights that contradict matte gouache
prompt_template: Flat opaque gouache illustration of {subject} in {setting}, matte chalky colour shapes with crisp edges, faint brush streaks, limited {palette}, {lighting} shown as simple flat value steps, {composition}, space left for text, no text.
prompt_example: Flat opaque gouache illustration of a person cleaning their glasses with a microfibre cloth at a café table, matte chalky colour shapes with crisp edges, faint brush streaks, limited palette of deep green, snow white, warm grey and a peach accent, soft window light shown as two flat value steps, subject on the right third with open space on the left, no text.
avoid_phrases: in the style of <any living artist>
flux_notes: FLUX leans to clean vector-flat; adding 'matte gouache, brush streaks, paper grain' helps. Hands holding glasses often break; keep hands simple or out of frame.

copying a specific famous picture-book look

name: Classical Oil Painting
name_th: สีน้ำมันคลาสสิก
historical_background: Layered oil painting on panel and canvas dominated European art from the Renaissance, which began in Italy around 1400 with its High Renaissance c.1500–1530 (Tate, 'Renaissance'). The classical method of underpainting, glazing and blended modelling persisted in academies into the nineteenth century.
visual_characteristics: Smooth blended modelling, deep transparent shadows, rich glazes, polished finish.
line_characteristics: No visible line; forms turn through soft gradations; edges varied from soft to crisp.
shape_language: Naturalistic, idealised proportions; stable pyramidal groupings.
color_characteristics: Earth-based palette (ochres, umbers, vermilion, ultramarine), warm lights and cool transparent darks.
lighting_characteristics: Single directional light, often north-window or chiaroscuro modelling.
texture_characteristics: Fine canvas weave, smooth glaze surface, slight craquelure on aged look.
composition_characteristics: Balanced, often triangular or centred; dark backgrounds isolating the subject.
time_optic_fit: Can lend prestige to a luxury frame campaign (portrait wearing the frame), but heavy and old-fashioned for daily posts; keep sparse.
common_mistakes: plastic airbrushed skin calling itself oil
modern glasses rendered as melted shapes
orange-brown 'old master' filter instead of real temperature control
prompt_template: Classical oil painting of {subject} in {setting}, smooth blended modelling with transparent glazes, warm lights and cool deep shadows, {palette}, {lighting}, {composition}, fine canvas texture, no text.
prompt_example: Classical oil painting portrait of a middle-aged Thai man wearing thin gold round glasses, seated in a dark-panelled study, smooth blended modelling with transparent glazes, warm lights and cool deep shadows, ochre, umber and deep green palette, single north-window light from the left, triangular half-length composition, fine canvas texture, no text.
avoid_phrases: in the style of <any living artist>
flux_notes: Gets the general look; glasses on painted faces often lose a temple arm or warp lens shape. Use a real frame reference via Codex -i when the frame must be accurate.

name: Oil Impasto
name_th: สีน้ำมันปาดหนา
historical_background: Impasto is paint laid on so thickly that it forms a raised, textured surface; Tate cites Titian, Tintoretto and Rubens, and modern examples such as Frank Auerbach's Head of E.O.W. I (1960), noting moderns valued it for expressing emotion (Tate, 'Impasto').
visual_characteristics: Thick ridged strokes, palette-knife slabs, paint catching real light, energetic surface.
line_characteristics: Lines are stroke edges; directional brushwork describes form.
color_characteristics: Juicy, high-chroma strokes placed side by side, partially mixed on the canvas.
lighting_characteristics: Strong directional light emphasising stroke relief.
texture_characteristics: Raised paint ridges, knife marks, broken colour.
composition_characteristics: Bold, simple; surface energy carries the image.
time_optic_fit: Works as an abstract textured background for colourful frames; poor for any detail-critical product or face.
prompt_template: Thick oil impasto painting of {subject} in {setting}, heavy palette-knife and brush strokes with raised paint ridges, {palette}, {lighting} raking across the paint relief, {composition}, no text.
prompt_example: Thick oil impasto painting of an abstract summer sea and sky as a backdrop, heavy palette-knife strokes with raised paint ridges, turquoise, deep green and peach palette, warm side light raking across the paint relief, low horizon with large sky area for a product cutout, no text.

texture_characteristics: Paper grain, blending-stump smoothness, graphite shine.
composition_characteristics: Subject on white, often vignetted; close studies.

composition_characteristics: Detailed focal area fading to open paper.

name: Woodcut Print

visual_characteristics: Bold black shapes, gouged white lines, visible wood grain in solids, high contrast.
line_characteristics: Chunky carved lines with V- and U-gouge marks; tapered cuts.
color_characteristics: Black on off-white; optional one or two flat colours from extra blocks, slight mis-registration.

texture_characteristics: Wood grain, uneven ink coverage, paper texture.
composition_characteristics: Strong graphic framing; dense pattern areas balanced by solids.
time_optic_fit: Works for wooden/handmade frame stories and bold posters; low detail means the real frame should be a photo layer.

name: Linocut
name_th: ภาพพิมพ์ลิโนเลียม
historical_background: Linocut carves a design into linoleum (usually wood-mounted), inks the raised areas and presses them onto paper; linoleum has no grain so it cuts in any direction and inks evenly; invented in the nineteenth century as flooring, it became popular for printmaking in the twentieth (Tate, 'Linocut').
visual_characteristics: Bold flat shapes, smooth even ink solids, carved line textures, graphic contrast.

name: Etching and Engraving
name_th: ภาพพิมพ์กัดกรด/แกะโลหะ
historical_background: Etching coats a metal plate (traditionally copper, now usually zinc) with an acid-resistant ground; lines scratched through it are bitten by acid, inked and printed; metal etching decoration dates from the fourteenth century and printmaking use became common in the early sixteenth (Tate, 'Etching'). Engraving cuts lines directly with a burin.
visual_characteristics: Very fine dense lines, cross-hatching and stipple, plate tone, crisp blacks.

color_characteristics: Black, sepia or sanguine ink on cream paper; optional hand-tinting.
lighting_characteristics: Value through line density; dramatic or even.
texture_characteristics: Plate mark border, ink tone wiping, soft paper.
composition_characteristics: Framed vignette, plate border, classical arrangement.

name: Art Deco

historical_background: Art deco flourished in the 1920s–30s in furniture, decorative arts and architecture; it took its name from the 1925 Paris International Exhibition of Modern Decorative and Industrial Arts, and, unlike art nouveau, was shaped by cubism and drew on Egyptian and Central American art and modern transport design (Tate, 'Art deco').
visual_characteristics: Geometric symmetry, sunbursts, stepped forms, chevrons, metallic accents.
line_characteristics: Crisp straight lines, fine parallel pinstripes, arcs.
color_characteristics: Black, gold, cream, emerald/jade, deep teal.
lighting_characteristics: Glossy highlights on metal and lacquer; dramatic uplight.
texture_characteristics: Lacquer, brass, marble, glass.
composition_characteristics: Symmetrical, vertical, radiating sunbursts.
time_optic_fit: Strong fit for premium/gold frames — black, gold and deep green echo brand phthalo green.
prompt_template: Art deco design of {subject} in {setting}, geometric symmetry, sunburst and stepped motifs, fine gold pinstripes, lacquer and brass surfaces, {palette}, {lighting}, {composition}, no text.

name: Bauhaus Modernist
name_th: โมเดิร์นนิสม์บาวเฮาส์
historical_background: The Bauhaus was founded by Walter Gropius in Weimar in 1919, moved to Dessau in 1925–26 and Berlin in 1932, and was closed by the Nazis in 1933; it gave architecture, design and applied arts equal weight with fine art, with teachers including Kandinsky, Klee, Moholy-Nagy and Albers (Tate, 'Bauhaus').
visual_characteristics: Primary shapes (circle, square, triangle), grids, asymmetrical layouts, sans-serif-ready space.
line_characteristics: Straight bars and rules, geometric arcs.
color_characteristics: Primary red, yellow, blue plus black/white/grey.
lighting_characteristics: Flat, no illusionistic light.
texture_characteristics: Smooth flat print, occasional paper grain.
composition_characteristics: Asymmetrical grid balance, diagonals, functional hierarchy.
time_optic_fit: Very usable as a layout logic for HTML carousels (grids, geometric frame shapes = round/square/cat-eye); swap primaries for brand tokens.
prompt_template: Bauhaus-inspired modernist composition of {subject}, built from circles, squares, triangles and bars on an asymmetric grid, flat {palette} colours, {composition}, generous clean space, no text.
prompt_example: Bauhaus-inspired modernist composition representing three frame shapes — a circle, a square and a soft triangle — built from flat geometric shapes and bars on an asymmetric grid, deep green, peach, snow white and raisin black, diagonal balance across the canvas, generous clean space, no text.

name: Constructivism
name_th: คอนสตรักติวิสม์
historical_background: Constructivism emerged in Russia around 1915, founded by Tatlin and Rodchenko; a manifesto appeared in Lef in 1923 and the movement was suppressed in Russia during the 1920s, with Gabo and Pevsner carrying its ideas west; it held art should reflect the modern industrial world (Tate, 'Constructivism').
visual_characteristics: Diagonal bold geometry, photomontage, red/black on cream, dynamic angles.
line_characteristics: Thick bars, rules, arrows.
shape_language: Rectangles, circles, wedges in dynamic tension.
color_characteristics: Red, black, cream, occasional grey.
lighting_characteristics: Flat graphic; high-contrast photo fragments.
texture_characteristics: Printed paper, halftone photo.
composition_characteristics: Strong diagonals, low-angle photos, radial thrust.

name: Surrealism
name_th: เซอร์เรียลิสม์
historical_background: Apollinaire coined 'surrealism' in a 1917 play preface, and André Breton's Surrealist Manifesto (1924) defined it as 'pure psychic automatism'; the Paris-based group drew on dreams and the unconscious through automatic drawing and writing (Tate, 'Surrealism').
visual_characteristics: Dream logic, impossible juxtapositions, realistic rendering of irrational scenes, long shadows.
line_characteristics: Precise rendering (veristic) or automatic loose line.
shape_language: Familiar objects in unfamiliar scale or context.
color_characteristics: Clear, often desert/sky tones; or dark dream palettes.
lighting_characteristics: Low raking light, long shadows, eerie stillness.
texture_characteristics: Smooth precise paint.
composition_characteristics: Deep empty spaces, low horizon, scale contrast.
use_cases: conceptual frame ads (giant glasses in landscape)
time_optic_fit: Strong for conceptual product ads (eye/vision metaphors, giant lenses showing a sharp world); avoid copying famous melting clocks or apple-face images.
prompt_template: Surrealist painting of {subject} in {setting}, dreamlike impossible juxtaposition rendered with precise realism, long raking shadows, eerie stillness, {palette}, {lighting}, {composition}, no text.
prompt_example: Surrealist painting of a giant pair of round glasses standing upright in a calm desert, the lenses showing a sharp green forest while the world around is blurred, precise realism, long raking evening shadows, eerie stillness, sand, sky blue and deep green palette, low horizon with the glasses centred, no text.

line_characteristics: Thick black outlines.

lighting_characteristics: Flat, graphic.
texture_characteristics: Printed dots, screenprint layers.
composition_characteristics: Central icon, grids of repetition.

historical_background: Op art was a major 1960s painting movement using geometric forms to create optical effects based on colour theory and the psychology of perception, ranging from subtle to disorienting; Vasarely was among its originators (Tate, 'Op art').

line_characteristics: Crisp parallel lines, concentric rings, warped grids.
color_characteristics: Black and white or high-contrast complementary pairs.

texture_characteristics: Flat hard-edge paint.
composition_characteristics: All-over patterns with a distortion zone.

name: Minimalism
name_th: มินิมอลลิสม์
historical_background: Minimalism emerged in the late 1950s in the USA and flourished in the 1960s–70s; Frank Stella's Black Paintings were shown at MoMA in 1959; works use simple geometric forms, make no attempt to depict outside reality, and drew on Russian constructivist and suprematist ideas (Tate, 'Minimalism').
visual_characteristics: Very few elements, large empty fields, precise geometry, restrained palette.
line_characteristics: Clean straight edges or none.
color_characteristics: Monochrome or two-colour; neutral or one saturated field.
lighting_characteristics: Even soft; in photography, gentle gradient.
texture_characteristics: Smooth, matte.
composition_characteristics: Negative space dominant; centred or strict grid.
time_optic_fit: Excellent: matches brand tokens (Snow, Timberwolf, Phthalo) and lets a single frame photo breathe.

name: Abstract Expressionism
name_th: แอบสแตรกต์เอ็กซ์เพรสชันนิสม์
historical_background: Abstract expressionism emerged in the 1940s–50s among New York painters (the New York school), in two tendencies: action painting with sweeping gestural marks and colour field painting with large areas of single colour, drawing on surrealist automatism (Tate, 'Abstract expressionism').
visual_characteristics: Large gestural marks, drips and splatters, or vast soft-edged colour fields.
line_characteristics: Energetic gestural strokes, drips; or none in colour field.

color_characteristics: Bold contrasts (action) or deep resonant fields (colour field).
lighting_characteristics: Not depicted.

composition_characteristics: All-over or large stacked fields.

name: Ukiyo-e Woodblock
name_th: ภาพพิมพ์แกะไม้อุกิโยเอะ
historical_background: Ukiyo-e, 'pictures of the floating world', depicted the entertainment districts of Edo-period Japan (the V&A dates the period 1615–1868); in 1765 multi-block printing was perfected, producing full-colour nishiki-e ('brocade pictures'), each colour carved on its own block and aligned with registration marks, made by publisher, designer, block cutter and printer (V&A). Tate notes ukiyo-e were printed by hand pressure rather than a press (Tate, 'Woodcut').
visual_characteristics: Flat areas of colour, elegant key-block outlines, patterned textiles, stylised waves and clouds, flattened space.
line_characteristics: Fine, confident black key-block line with graceful taper.
color_characteristics: Soft natural-pigment tones (indigo/Prussian blue, vermilion, soft yellows) with gradient wiping in skies.
lighting_characteristics: No cast shadows; flat decorative light.
texture_characteristics: Washi paper fibre, embossing, woodgrain in flat areas.
composition_characteristics: Asymmetric, high or tilted viewpoints, dramatic cropping, foreground framing elements.
time_optic_fit: Use respectfully as technique (flat colour, key line, gradient sky) for travel or rain-season content; avoid fake Japanese text/seals and imitations of famous prints (great wave).

name: Thai Traditional Mural
name_th: จิตรกรรมฝาผนังไทย
historical_background: Siamese Buddhist murals in temples and palaces were standardised in the Rattanakosin (Bangkok) period after eighteenth-century experimentation, with marked change under King Rama III (c.1824–51); main subjects are Jataka tales of the Buddha's past lives, Traiphum cosmology and the Ramakien, arranged in bays between windows and divided by zig-zag sinthao lines (Royal Thai Embassy Seoul article). Recent scholarship analyses the oblique (diagonal) structure of early Rattanakosin compositions (Thai journal abstract).
visual_characteristics: Continuous narrative scenes, flat figures in elegant gestures, pavilions and landscapes viewed obliquely, zig-zag dividers, gold accents.
line_characteristics: Fine fluid contour lines defining figures, flame-like (kranok) ornament.
shape_language: Stylised graceful figures; ornamented architecture; rocks and trees as patterns.
color_characteristics: Earthy mineral reds, ochres, greens, dark backgrounds with gold leaf highlights (colour terms are general observation; the opened source does not detail pigments).
lighting_characteristics: No cast shadows; flat even light.
texture_characteristics: Aged wall plaster, fine cracks, gold leaf sheen.
composition_characteristics: Many scenes on one wall, oblique bird's-eye layout, sinthao zig-zag separators, registers.
use_cases: Songkran/cultural greetings using secular village-life motifs only
story clips set in old Thailand with secular scenes
time_optic_fit: Handle with care. Temple murals are sacred Buddhist art: never put the Buddha, monks, deities or Jataka scenes in a sales ad, never put glasses on sacred figures. Acceptable: secular village/market scenes, ornament-inspired borders, educational posts crediting the tradition. Prefer consulting the user before using it for promotion.
common_mistakes: using Buddha or sacred figures as decoration in ads
putting sunglasses on deities or monks

prompt_example: Painting in the manner of a traditional Thai mural (secular scene) of a lively riverside floating market with villagers trading fruit from boats, flat figures with fine fluid contours, elegant stylised gestures, oblique bird's-eye arrangement with zig-zag dividing lines, earthy reds, ochres and deep greens with small gold accents, flat even light, several small scenes across a wide panel, aged plaster texture, no religious figures, no text.
